 478 │ 478 │     """                                                                                    
 479 │ 479 │     Yields the platform tags for an iOS system.                                            
 480 │ 480 │

 490 │ 490 │         # it won't exist for CPython versions before 3.13, which causes a mypy             
 491 │ 491 │         # error.

 496 │ 496 │         multiarch = sys.implementation._multiarch

 191 │ 191 │ def _parse_project_urls(data: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:                                   
 192 │ 192 │     """Parse a list of label/URL string pairings separated by a comma."""                     
 193 │ 193 │     urls = {}                                                                                 
 194 │ 194 │     for pair in data:                                                                         
 195 │ 195 │         # Our logic is slightly tricky here as we want to try and do                          
 196 │ 196 │         # *something* reasonable with malformed data.                                         
 197 │ 197 │         #                                                                                     
 198 │ 198 │         # The main thing that we have to worry about, is data that does                       
 199 │ 199 │         # not have a ',' at all to split the label from the Value. There                      
 200 │ 200 │         # isn't a singular right answer here, and we will fail validation                     
 201 │ 201 │         # later on (if the caller is validating) so it doesn't *really*                       
 202 │ 202 │         # matter, but since the missing value has to be an empty str                          
 203 │ 203 │         # and our return value is dict[str, str], if we let the key                           
 204 │ 204 │         # be the missing value, then they'd have multiple '' values that                      
 205 │ 205 │         # overwrite each other in a accumulating dict.                                        
 206 │ 206 │         #                                                                                     
 207 │ 207 │         # The other potential issue is that it's possible to have the                         
 208 │ 208 │         # same label multiple times in the metadata, with no solid "right"                    
 209 │ 209 │         # answer with what to do in that case. As such, we'll do the only                     
 210 │ 210 │         # thing we can, which is treat the field as unparsable and add it                     
 211 │ 211 │         # to our list of unparsed fields.                                                     
 212 │ 212 │         #                                                                                     
 213 │ 213 │         # TODO: The spec doesn't say anything about if the keys should be                     
 214 │ 214 │         #       considered case sensitive or not... logically they should                     
 215 │ 215 │         #       be case-preserving and case-insensitive, but doing that                       
 216 │ 216 │         #       would open up more cases where we might have duplicate                        
 217 │ 217 │         #       entries.                                                                      
 218 │ 218 │         label, _, url = (s.strip() for s in pair.partition(","))                              
 219 │ 219 │                                                                                               
 220 │ 220 │         if label in urls:                                                                     
 221 │ 221 │             # The label already exists in our set of urls, so this field                      
 222 │ 222 │             # is unparsable, and we can just add the whole thing to our                       
 223 │ 223 │             # unparsable data and stop processing it.                                         
 224 │ 224 │             raise KeyError("duplicate labels in project urls")                                
 225 │ 225 │         urls[label] = url                                                                     
 226 │ 226 │                                                                                               
 227 │ 227 │     return urls

 232 │ 232 │     # If our source is a str, then our caller has managed encodings for us,

 246 │ 246 │             raise ValueError("payload in an invalid encoding") from exc

 338 │ 338 │     """Parse a distribution's metadata stored as email headers (e.g. from ``METADATA``).      
 339 │ 339 │

 342 │ 342 │     parsed and translated into Python's built-in types are converted                          
 343 │ 343 │     appropriately. All other fields are left as-is. Fields that are allowed to                
 344 │ 344 │     appear multiple times are stored as lists.                                                
 345 │ 345 │                                                                                               
 346 │ 346 │     The second dict contains all other fields from the metadata. This includes                
 347 │ 347 │     any unrecognized fields. It also includes any fields which are expected to                
 348 │ 348 │     be parsed into a built-in type but were not formatted appropriately. Finally,             
 349 │ 349 │     any fields that are expected to appear only once but are repeated are                     
 350 │ 350 │     included in this dict.                                                                    
 351 │ 351 │                                                                                               
 352 │ 352 │     """

 356 │ 356 │     if isinstance(data, str):

 362 │ 362 │     # values for a key (a list), the key will appear multiple times in the                    
 363 │ 363 │     # list of keys, but we're avoiding that by using get_all().                               
 364 │ 364 │     for name_with_case in frozenset(parsed.keys()):                                           
 365 │ 365 │         # Header names in RFC are case insensitive, so we'll normalize to all                 
 366 │ 366 │         # lower case to make comparisons easier.                                              
 367 │ 367 │         name = name_with_case.lower()                                                         
 368 │ 368 │                                                                                               
 369 │ 369 │         # We use get_all() here, even for fields that aren't multiple use,                    
 370 │ 370 │         # because otherwise someone could have e.g. two Name fields, and we                   
 371 │ 371 │         # would just silently ignore it rather than doing something about it.

 375 │ 375 │         # unconditionally decodes the bytes as ascii using the surrogateescape                
 376 │ 376 │         # handler. When you pull that data back out (such as with get_all() ),                
 377 │ 377 │         # it looks to see if the str has any surrogate escapes, and if it does

 386 │ 386 │             # It's unclear if this can return more types than just a Header or

 390 │ 390 │             # If it's a header object, we need to do our little dance to get

 394 │ 394 │             # ourselves.                                                                      
 395 │ 395 │             #

 528 │ 528 │ class _Validator(Generic[T]):                                                                 
 529 │ 529 │     """Validate a metadata field.                                                             
 530 │ 530 │                                                                                               
 531 │ 531 │     All _process_*() methods correspond to a core metadata field. The method is               
 532 │ 532 │     called with the field's raw value. If the raw value is valid it is returned               
 533 │ 533 │     in its "enriched" form (e.g. ``version.Version`` for the ``Version`` field).              
 534 │ 534 │     If the raw value is invalid, :exc:`InvalidMetadata` is raised (with a cause               
 535 │ 535 │     as appropriate).                                                                          
 536 │ 536 │     """                                                                                       
 537 │ 537 │                                                                                               
 538 │ 538 │     name: str                                                                                 
 539 │ 539 │     raw_name: str                                                                             
 540 │ 540 │     added: _MetadataVersion                                                                   
 541 │ 541 │                                                                                               
 542 │ 542 │     def __init__(                                                                             
 543 │ 543 │         self,                                                                                 
 544 │ 544 │         *,                                                                                    
 545 │ 545 │         added: _MetadataVersion = "1.0",                                                      
 546 │ 546 │     ) -> None:                                                                                
 547 │ 547 │         self.added = added                                                                    
 548 │ 548 │                                                                                               
 549 │ 549 │     def __set_name__(self, _owner: Metadata, name: str) -> None:                              
 550 │ 550 │         self.name = name                                                                      
 551 │ 551 │         self.raw_name = _RAW_TO_EMAIL_MAPPING[name]                                           
 552 │ 552 │                                                                                               
 553 │ 553 │     def __get__(self, instance: Metadata, _owner: type[Metadata]) -> T:                       
 554 │ 554 │         # With Python 3.8, the caching can be replaced with functools.cached_property().      
 555 │ 555 │         # No need to check the cache as attribute lookup will resolve into the                
 556 │ 556 │         # instance's __dict__ before __get__ is called.                                       
 557 │ 557 │         cache = instance.__dict__                                                             
 558 │ 558 │         value = instance._raw.get(self.name)                                                  
 559 │ 559 │                                                                                               
 560 │ 560 │         # To make the _process_* methods easier, we'll check if the value is None             
 561 │ 561 │         # and if this field is NOT a required attribute, and if both of those                 
 562 │ 562 │         # things are true, we'll skip the the converter. This will mean that the              
 563 │ 563 │         # converters never have to deal with the None union.                                  
 564 │ 564 │         if self.name in _REQUIRED_ATTRS or value is not None:                                 
 565 │ 565 │             try:                                                                              
 566 │ 566 │                 converter: Callable[[Any], T] = getattr(self, f"_process_{self.name}")        
 567 │ 567 │             except AttributeError:                                                            
 568 │ 568 │                 pass                                                                          
 569 │ 569 │             else:                                                                             
 570 │ 570 │                 value = converter(value)                                                      
 571 │ 571 │                                                                                               
 572 │ 572 │         cache[self.name] = value                                                              
 573 │ 573 │         try:                                                                                  
 574 │ 574 │             del instance._raw[self.name]  # type: ignore[misc]                                
 575 │ 575 │         except KeyError:                                                                      
 576 │ 576 │             pass                                                                              
 577 │ 577 │                                                                                               
 578 │ 578 │         return cast("T", value)                                                               
 579 │ 579 │                                                                                               
 580 │ 580 │     def _invalid_metadata(                                                                    
 581 │ 581 │         self, msg: str, cause: Exception | None = None                                        
 582 │ 582 │     ) -> InvalidMetadata:                                                                     
 583 │ 583 │         exc = InvalidMetadata(                                                                
 584 │ 584 │             self.raw_name, msg.format_map({"field": repr(self.raw_name)})                     
 585 │ 585 │         )                                                                                     
 586 │ 586 │         exc.__cause__ = cause                                                                 
 587 │ 587 │         return exc                                                                            
 588 │ 588 │

 590 │ 590 │         # Implicitly makes Metadata-Version required.

 592 │ 592 │             raise self._invalid_metadata(f"{value!r} is not a valid metadata version")

 624 │ 624 │     def _process_description_content_type(self, value: str) -> str:                           
 625 │ 625 │         content_types = {"text/plain", "text/x-rst", "text/markdown"}                         
 626 │ 626 │         message = email.message.EmailMessage()

 635 │ 635 │         # not parseable.                                                                      
 636 │ 636 │         if content_type not in content_types or content_type not in value.lower():            
 637 │ 637 │             raise self._invalid_metadata(                                                     
 638 │ 638 │                 f"{{field}} must be one of {list(content_types)}, not {value!r}"              
 639 │ 639 │             )                                                                                 
 640 │ 640 │                                                                                               
 641 │ 641 │         charset = parameters.get("charset", "UTF-8")

 643 │ 643 │             raise self._invalid_metadata(                                                     
 644 │ 644 │                 f"{{field}} can only specify the UTF-8 charset, not {list(charset)}"          
 645 │ 645 │             )                                                                                 
 646 │ 646 │                                                                                               
 647 │ 647 │         markdown_variants = {"GFM", "CommonMark"}                                             
 648 │ 648 │         variant = parameters.get("variant", "GFM")  # Use an acceptable default.

 652 │ 652 │                 f"not {variant!r}",

 656 │ 656 │     def _process_dynamic(self, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:

 714 │ 714 │     def _process_license_files(self, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:                          
 715 │ 715 │         paths = []                                                                            
 716 │ 716 │         for path in value:                                                                    
 717 │ 717 │             if ".." in path:

 719 │ 719 │                     f"{path!r} is invalid for {{field}}, "                                    
 720 │ 720 │                     "parent directory indicators are not allowed"                             
 721 │ 721 │                 )

 723 │ 723 │                 raise self._invalid_metadata(                                                 
 724 │ 724 │                     f"{path!r} is invalid for {{field}}, paths must be resolved"              
 725 │ 725 │                 )

 727 │ 727 │                 pathlib.PurePosixPath(path).is_absolute()                                     
 728 │ 728 │                 or pathlib.PureWindowsPath(path).is_absolute()                                
 729 │ 729 │             ):

 731 │ 731 │                     f"{path!r} is invalid for {{field}}, paths must be relative"              
 732 │ 732 │                 )

 734 │ 734 │                 raise self._invalid_metadata(

 766 │ 766 │     """Representation of distribution metadata.                                               
 767 │ 767 │                                                                                               
 768 │ 768 │     Compared to :class:`RawMetadata`, this class provides objects representing                
 769 │ 769 │     metadata fields instead of only using built-in types. Any invalid metadata                
 770 │ 770 │     will cause :exc:`InvalidMetadata` to be raised (with a                                    
 771 │ 771 │     :py:attr:`~BaseException.__cause__` attribute as appropriate).                            
 772 │ 772 │     """                                                                                       
 773 │ 773 │                                                                                               
 774 │ 774 │     _raw: RawMetadata                                                                         
 775 │ 775 │                                                                                               
 776 │ 776 │     @classmethod                                                                              
 777 │ 777 │     def from_raw(cls, data: RawMetadata, *, validate: bool = True) -> Metadata:               
 778 │ 778 │         """Create an instance from :class:`RawMetadata`.                                      
 779 │ 779 │                                                                                               
 780 │ 780 │         If *validate* is true, all metadata will be validated. All exceptions                 
 781 │ 781 │         related to validation will be gathered and raised as an :class:`ExceptionGroup`.      
 782 │ 782 │         """                                                                                   
 783 │ 783 │         ins = cls()                                                                           
 784 │ 784 │         ins._raw = data.copy()  # Mutations occur due to caching enriched values.             
 785 │ 785 │                                                                                               
 786 │ 786 │         if validate:                                                                          
 787 │ 787 │             exceptions: list[Exception] = []                                                  
 788 │ 788 │             try:                                                                              
 789 │ 789 │                 metadata_version = ins.metadata_version                                       
 790 │ 790 │                 metadata_age = _VALID_METADATA_VERSIONS.index(metadata_version)               
 791 │ 791 │             except InvalidMetadata as metadata_version_exc:                                   
 792 │ 792 │                 exceptions.append(metadata_version_exc)                                       
 793 │ 793 │                 metadata_version = None                                                       
 794 │ 794 │                                                                                               
 795 │ 795 │             # Make sure to check for the fields that are present, the required                
 796 │ 796 │             # fields (so their absence can be reported).                                      
 797 │ 797 │             fields_to_check = frozenset(ins._raw) | _REQUIRED_ATTRS                           
 798 │ 798 │             # Remove fields that have already been checked.                                   
 799 │ 799 │             fields_to_check -= {"metadata_version"}                                           
 800 │ 800 │                                                                                               
 801 │ 801 │             for key in fields_to_check:                                                       
 802 │ 802 │                 try:                                                                          
 803 │ 803 │                     if metadata_version:                                                      
 804 │ 804 │                         # Can't use getattr() as that triggers descriptor protocol which      
 805 │ 805 │                         # will fail due to no value for the instance argument.                
 806 │ 806 │                         try:                                                                  
 807 │ 807 │                             field_metadata_version = cls.__dict__[key].added                  
 808 │ 808 │                         except KeyError:                                                      
 809 │ 809 │                             exc = InvalidMetadata(key, f"unrecognized field: {key!r}")        
 810 │ 810 │                             exceptions.append(exc)                                            
 811 │ 811 │                             continue                                                          
 812 │ 812 │                         field_age = _VALID_METADATA_VERSIONS.index(                           
 813 │ 813 │                             field_metadata_version                                            
 814 │ 814 │                         )                                                                     
 815 │ 815 │                         if field_age > metadata_age:                                          
 816 │ 816 │                             field = _RAW_TO_EMAIL_MAPPING[key]                                
 817 │ 817 │                             exc = InvalidMetadata(                                            
 818 │ 818 │                                 field,                                                        
 819 │ 819 │                                 f"{field} introduced in metadata version "                    
 820 │ 820 │                                 f"{field_metadata_version}, not {metadata_version}",          
 821 │ 821 │                             )                                                                 
 822 │ 822 │                             exceptions.append(exc)                                            
 823 │ 823 │                             continue                                                          
 824 │ 824 │                     getattr(ins, key)                                                         
 825 │ 825 │                 except InvalidMetadata as exc:                                                
 826 │ 826 │                     exceptions.append(exc)                                                    
 827 │ 827 │                                                                                               
 828 │ 828 │             if exceptions:                                                                    
 829 │ 829 │                 raise ExceptionGroup("invalid metadata", exceptions)                          
 830 │ 830 │                                                                                               
 831 │ 831 │         return ins
